interest: Shows 1930s American firms fighting Japanese patent and trademark infringement, including Singer's SIMANCO counterfeits, amid growing wartime trade controls.
overview: This file comprises State Department 'List of Papers' docket sheets for decimal file 894.542, spanning from 1930 to 1939, recording official correspondence, legal memoranda, and cross-references regarding patents, patent infringements, and industrial property rights in Japan. The documents trace complaints brought by American firms and inventors—including General Printing Ink Corporation, General Reduction Corporation, Pridwin Industries, Prophylactic Toothbrush Company, A. Sauer and Company, and Singer Manufacturing Company—concerning unauthorized duplication of American machinery, tools, and consumer goods by Japanese competitors, as well as Japanese legislative developments such as the Unfair Competition Law of 1934 and the 1938 Patent Law revision. Throughout these cases, the State Department consistently maintained that it lacked authority to intervene diplomatically without clear treaty violations or local branch establishment under Japanese law, advising aggrieved American businesses to retain private local counsel or pursue domestic legal remedies such as customs exclusions and federal court injunctions.

subfiles.about: Docket register sheets recording correspondence and cross-references regarding Japanese patent legislation, unfair competition laws, and inquiries concerning protection for American inventions between 1933 and 1938.
subfiles.summary: Lists 1933-38 patent matters: Bulkley's Japan plant-visit inquiry, Garrels on Japan's Unfair Competition Law, White's rug-machine and Cookingham's and Cabell's cases, and Grew transmitting Japan's revised 1938 Patent Law.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Patents — Japan (894.542/6 to 894.542/16)

subfiles.about: Docket sheet summarizing the 1930 case regarding alleged infringement of General Printing Ink Corporation's machinery patents by Japanese companies in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: General Printing Ink's complaint that Japanese firms copied its lithograph press and oven patents was denied diplomatic help under treaty law; State offered Tokyo legal-counsel contacts instead.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Patent of General Printing Ink Corporation in Japan

subfiles.about: Docket sheet recording the 1931 case concerning the Japanese government's refusal to grant metallurgical patents to the General Reduction Corporation.
subfiles.summary: Attorneys for General Reduction Corporation sought protests after Japan rejected two patent applications, but withdrew once State asked for more details, deciding the patents weren't worth contesting.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Protection of Patent Rights of General Reduction Corporation in Japan

subfiles.about: Docket sheet summarizing 1934 communications regarding alleged patent violations in Japan affecting Pridwin Industries Company.
subfiles.summary: Garrels forwarded Pridwin Industries' patent infringement complaint against Japanese concerns; Legal Adviser Ward approved an unusual direct forward of the Consul's letter given developing circumstances.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Protection of Patents of Pridwin Industries Company in Japan

subfiles.about: Docket sheet recording 1934 interdepartmental coordination regarding patent and trademark infringements of Prophylactic Toothbrush Company products in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Dooman and Commerce's Brown discussed Prophylactic Toothbrush Company's patent and trademark infringement by Japanese manufacturers, with infringing packages and labels forwarded for review.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Infringement of Patents of the Prophylactic Toothbrush Company by Japanese Manufacturers

subfiles.about: Docket sheet summarizing the 1935 case regarding the copying and importation of A. Sauer and Company's patented tubular watch straps.
subfiles.summary: Senator Donahey's constituent A. Sauer sought to stop cheap Japanese tubular-watch-strap imports; State found no diplomatic basis since the goods were legal under Japanese law, suggesting court injunctions or Treasury exclusion petitions instead.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Infringement of Patents of A. Sauer and Company by Japanese Manufacturers

subfiles.about: Docket sheet recording complaints, international investigations, and wartime economic restrictions involving Singer sewing machine patents, trademarks, and Japanese branch operations from 1934 to 1939.
subfiles.summary: Singer's 1934-39 case: the Japanese Legation in Lisbon distributed circulars for counterfeit 'SIMANCO'-branded parts, and by 1938-39 wartime import and exchange controls strained Singer's Japanese branch, ending in talks on blocked yen with Hornbeck.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Infringement of Singer Manufacturing Company's Patent by Japanese
